UserAdminOut.description: What admins see when managing users: includes activity so deletion can be an informed choice.
UserAdminOut.title: UserAdminOut

get.description:
Google redirects here. Signs in the existing, active user whose email Google has verified.
Every failure redirects to /login?error=... with a generic code (no hint whether an account exists).
Start Google sign-in: sets a short-lived signed cookie and redirects to Google.

put.description:
Change your own password. Every other session of yours is signed out; this one stays signed in.

A wrong current password is a 400, not a 401: the web client treats 401 as "session expired".

get.description: Which sign-in methods are configured, so the login page knows whether to show the Google button.

schema.title: Response List Users Auth Users Get

delete.description:
Permanently delete a user. Their paper assignments are removed. If they have reviewed grades the
delete is refused (deactivate instead, which keeps the attribution) unless force=true, which keeps
the grades but clears who reviewed them.

patch.description:
Change a user's role, active flag and/or name. Takes effect immediately: the session cookie holds
only the user id, and role/active are read from the database on every request.

put.description:
Admin sets a user's password directly without requiring the current password.
All other sessions of that user are signed out; if resetting your own, this session stays signed in.

delete.description:
Permanently delete an exam: all rubric versions and every paper in it (grades, page images, stored PDFs).
An exam that still has papers needs force=true. Students are kept.

get.description:
Every paper of the exam as PDFs in a ZIP: graded papers annotated, ungraded ones as the original scan. `ids` (comma-separated submission ids) limits it to those
papers. `raw=true` exports the ORIGINAL scans of every paper (or of `ids`), graded or not.

post.description:
Two layouts:
  - one PDF per student, named `<student_id>.pdf`
  - one combined PDF + a CSV giving each student's `first_page`/`last_page`
Call with dry_run=true first to preview, then repeat with dry_run=false to commit.

schema.title: Response List Auto Splits Exams  Exam Id  Imports Auto Split Get

post.description:
Upload one combined PDF (and optionally a roster CSV) and queue a background job for Claude to propose splits
& roll numbers.
Grade everything that hasn't been graded: queue every submission that is uploaded or failed.
A PDF of the rubric JSON you send (so unsaved edits can be printed too), generated on the fly. Nothing is stored.
Rubrics are immutable; editing creates a new version so past grading runs stay traceable.

get.description: Is the grading backend usable? (e.g. is Claude logged in?) Shown as a banner to admins.

post.description:
Check the remaining quota now. Sends one tiny Haiku request (through the runner), so it is a POST and the UI
only calls it when an admin presses the button.

patch.description: Correct a student's roll number (external_id) and/or name.

put.description: Assign TAs to several papers at once: replace each paper's TAs, add to them, or remove from them.

post.description:
Permanently delete several papers (see DELETE /submissions/{id}). All or nothing: if any is being graded, or
any holds TA-reviewed grades and force is false, nothing is deleted.

Start grading (or regrading) the chosen papers with the latest rubric. Papers already queued or being
graded are skipped, and so are papers with TA-reviewed grades unless force=true.

delete.description:
Permanently delete one paper: its grades, page images, grading history and assignments, and the
stored PDF. The student record stays. A paper with TA-reviewed grades needs force=true.

get.description:
The graded PDF (marks and comments beside the pages, summary page in front). A paper that is not graded yet
(uploaded, queued, being graded or failed) has nothing to show, so the original scan is returned instead.
The original scan exactly as it was uploaded, graded or not.
